preamble: Stopping of the voiced alveolar fricative [z] to [d] is rare as a regular change. The best-documented case is Southern and South Midland American English, where /z/ becomes [d] before a syllabic or unstressed /n/ (isn't, wasn't, business).

examples.note: Anticipation of the following nasal closure turns the sibilant into a stop; used across social classes in the South and South Midland.
Same conditioning: /z/ before syllabic or unstressed /n/.

sources: Dictionary.com / Random House Unabridged Dictionary (2025). isn't: pronunciation note. https://www.dictionary.com/browse/isn-t
